learning_outcomes.text: Describe and analyze feedback dynamic systems both in time and in frequency.
Design continuous and discrete regulators useful to improve the dynamical behavior of the controlled systems.
Learn the main methods of time and frequency analysis of linear dynamic systems and the synthesis of simple lead and lag networks.
Analyze the time and frequency dynamics of linear physical systems described by transfer functions.
Analyze and control linear physical systems.
Express the learned concepts with an appropriate language and to properly discuss the topics of the course.
Acquire the methodological tools to continue their studies and to be able to arrange their own update.

syllabus_topics: Dynamic models of some physical systems
Analysis of the first and second order systems
Frequency response of systems with dominant poles
Rules for the qualitative drawing of the Bode and Nyquist plots
General properties of the closed-loop systems
Sensitivity to disturbances and to parameters variations
Resonant frequency, resonant peak and bandwidth
Definition and properties of the Root-Locus
Rules for the graphical drawing of the Root-Locus
Design of lead and lag compensators
Design of a lead/lag compensator on the Nyquist and Nichols planes
Recap exercises about the course topics
teaching_methods: Lectures with slides and exercises done on the blackboard

assessment_methods.method: Additional point for Matlab OnRamp course completion

assessment_rules: The final mark is the average of the two best positive-rated marks from the two partial written exams (Controls A and Controls B), plus an additional point for completing the Matlab OnRamp course with a certificate. The maximum mark is 33 points, with Laude granted for more than 31.5 points. Students who do not wish to take partial exams may opt for an oral exam, which consists of theoretical questions, numerical exercises, and qualitative analyses for Controls A and Controls B separately, each lasting approximately 30 minutes.
